SG-2 (no exported severity order) — VERIFIED: core/types.ts:22 LOG_LEVELS is module-private and adapter/journal.ts:55 LEVEL_ORDER is a second private copy; the §7.1 order exists nowhere as an exported value. RESOLUTION: add the word `export` to core/types.ts:22 (`export const LOG_LEVELS`) and have replay import it. Reasoning: this is not a vocabulary or schema change — the identical list already ships inside SCHEMAS via logLevelSchema (types.ts:455), so nothing observable widens; and a replay-local copy would make three definitions of one order, which is exactly the failure §7.4 legislates against. adapter/journal.ts's private LEVEL_ORDER is deliberately LEFT ALONE: refactoring a committed adapter with 40+ journal tests is outside this task's file scope and would put a second red in the tree. The duplication is recorded here so a later cleanup task can collapse it; row 15.0-level-threshold asserts replay's order equals the exported core list rather than a literal.

SG-3 (the review verdict table has no verdicts to read) — §7.3:1950-1951 asks for 'review verdict tables' from the JOURNAL, but at HEAD no journal record carries a per-finding uphold/overturn verdict, and the §1.2:439 `reviews/<itemId|plan>-r<N>.json` file has NO writer in the tree. RESOLUTION: the table is a REVIEW ROUND table derived from the records that actually exist — 'fsm'/'guard-reject' with data.stage present (round, max, findings, survivingMajors) and 'fsm'/'transition' carrying data.survivingMajors (rounds, lenses, findingsRaised) — keyed by subject = record.itemId ?? 'plan', one row per round, plus the reviewer/skeptic sub-session counts in that round's window from the fan-out rows. Reasoning: a renderer must not invent data (a fabricated verdict column is worse than an absent one), and replay MUST NOT read reviews/*.json, because a tool that reads a file nobody writes is a stub (G4). The derivation is FIELD-SHAPED, not pinned to conductor_plan_review, so 9.5a's item-review rounds fall into it unchanged when they land. If the orchestrator later wants true per-finding verdicts in the timeline, the producer must journal them — that is a producer decision, not a replay one, and it is raised here rather than taken.

SG-4 (the producer drops the lens the plan's own example shows) — FanoutJob carries `lens?` (fanout.ts:63) and §7.2:1932-1936's example record includes `"lens": "correctness"`, but the committed dispatched payload (fanout.ts:281-289) omits it. RESOLUTION for 15.0: replay renders the lens when `data.lens` is present, otherwise falls back to the round's `data.lenses` roster from the plan-review transition record, otherwise marks the lens unknown — never fabricated (row 15.0-review-lens-tolerant). 15.0 does NOT edit adapter/fanout.ts: the one-line producer fix (`lens: job.lens` in the dispatched payload, a data-payload addition that isKnownEvent does not police) is RAISED for the orchestrator as a separate ledgered nit, because touching a committed adapter mid-Phase-9 would put a second red in a file three other tasks are queued on.

SG-5 (seq is not a global order) — VERIFIED at journal.ts:101-121 + :219: rotation truncates journal.jsonl, so the next process's readLastSeq returns 0 and seq RESTARTS. RESOLUTION: the timeline's order is source order — archives by ascending N first, then the active journal, and within each file its line order — never a sort by seq or by ts. Reasoning: append order is the only true causal order available; ts ties at millisecond resolution and seq repeats across rotation. The rendered row still shows the recorded seq verbatim (it is what a grep of the file will match), duplicates and all.

SG-6 (rotated archives unmentioned) — the Task 15.0 bullet says 'a fixture journal' and §7.3 says 'renders a journal', but §7.1:1920-1921 makes journal.N.jsonl.gz a normal state of a long run. RESOLUTION: readRunJournal reads every journal.<N>.jsonl.gz in ascending N (gunzipSync, node:zlib — the same module journal.ts:26 gzips with) before journal.jsonl. An archive that cannot be read or inflated is reported as a failed source in the render header and the remaining sources still render, exit 0 — a partially readable history is still worth reading, and a silent omission would make the timeline lie about what happened.

SG-7 (no exit-code table) — §7.3 specifies none; Task 15.1:3040 says OPERATIONS.md will carry 'exit-code and error-envelope tables', so 15.0 must define what 15.1 documents. RESOLUTION, pinned by row 15.0-cli-exit-codes: 0 = rendered (including an empty journal, which renders an explicit zero-record notice); 2 = usage error (no run-dir argument, unknown flag, unknown --component/--level value) with the message on stderr and NOTHING on stdout; 1 = the run dir exists but holds no readable journal source at all, naming the path. Malformed lines and failed archives do NOT change the exit code — they are reported inside the render.

SG-8 (flag multiplicity and semantics undefined) — §7.3:1948-1949 shows `[--component …] [--level …] [--item I3]` and nothing more. RESOLUTION: --component and --item may each be repeated AND comma-separated, values unioned within a flag; the three flags compose as AND; --level is a THRESHOLD (at-or-above severity, matching §7.1's sink semantics), not an exact match, and defaults to no filtering; --item selects records whose itemId is in the set, which EXCLUDES run-level records (they have no itemId and belong to the run lane, not to item I3). Filters are applied ONCE, and every section derives from that one filtered set (row 15.0-filters-applied-once) — a swimlane and a duration table disagreeing about which records exist would be worse than either alone.

SG-9 (what 'highlighted' means) — RESOLUTION: plain-ASCII markers, no ANSI escape sequences anywhere in the output. Reasoning: G1 forbids a color dependency, replay output is routinely piped into a file or a bug report, and a test can only assert on deterministic bytes. `gates`/`deny` is marked DENY; `gates`/`gate-crash` is marked CRASH and listed in the same section with a distinct marker — an error-level fail-closed crash (tools.ts:240-252) is the one record class a reader must not miss, and §7.3's 'denials highlighted' plainly covers the case where the gate did not even get to decide. Both markers are distinct strings so each is independently assertable.

SG-10 (tools/ is unguarded) — VERIFIED: tests/purity.test.ts:27-29 scans core/, adapter/ and plugin/ only, so no committed guard covers conductor/tools/. RESOLUTION: 15.0's own test file carries the G1/G14 hygiene row for replay.ts (row 15.0-builtins-only) rather than widening purity.test.ts. Reasoning: purity.test.ts is Task 1.4's file, and one owner per test file is what keeps a red attributable; widening 1.4's globs to tools/ is a strictly better long-term answer and is RAISED for the orchestrator as a follow-up, not taken here.

SG-11 (Phase 15 runs after phases that are not built) — 9.5a is in flight and 9.5b/9.5c/9.6/10.1/12/13/14 are NOT_STARTED, so publish, report and item-review records do not exist to render. RESOLUTION: no row asserts on an uncommitted producer's payload. Every fixture in this spec is built from records the COMMITTED producers emit today (journal.ts, fanout.ts, tools.ts 9.1-9.4b), and the derivations are field-shaped so later producers' records fall into the right lane and table without a code change. Consequence: 15.0 has no build-order dependency and could be built at any point after Phase 7; it is scheduled in Phase 15 by the plan, not by a dependency.

SG-12 (what 'a fixture journal' is) — RESOLUTION: the tests build their own fixtures — literal JSONL text for the pure derivations, and for readRunJournal a temp dir written with node:fs plus a real gzipSync archive (mirroring tests/export-schemas.test.ts:33-40's mkdtemp/rmSync discipline). No recorded run, no model, no network, no dependency on another task's artifacts. Two rows additionally cross-check the fixture against reality by driving the COMMITTED createJournal (adapter/journal.ts:161) to produce the file replay then reads, so the fixture shape can never drift from what the writer actually writes.

assertions.text: conductor/tools/replay.ts exports exactly the SG-1 surface — parseJournalText, applyFilters, deriveSwimlanes, deriveFanoutRows, deriveReviewRounds, renderTimeline, parseArgs, readRunJournal — and importing the module is SIDE-EFFECT FREE: the import writes nothing to stdout or stderr, creates and reads no file, and the CLI leg fires only when process.argv[1] ends with 'replay.ts' (the committed tools/export-schemas.ts:39 guard, not import.meta.main, because Node type-stripping does not provide it and the file must also load under Bun)

parseJournalText returns one JournalRecord per well-formed line, in FILE ORDER (asserted by comparing the returned seq/event sequence to the fixture's line sequence), with blank and whitespace-only lines skipped silently — a blank line is not a malformed record — and it never throws for any input, including empty text (which yields zero records and zero malformed entries)

a TORN line — the fixture shape adapter/journal.ts:129-139 heals, i.e. a truncated JSON fragment followed by a newline and then complete records — is reported in malformed[] with its 1-based line number, the raw text, and a reason naming the JSON parse failure, while every complete record on the other lines is still returned. The torn fragment is never silently dropped (§7.4) and never crashes the parse

a line that is valid JSON but not a valid journal record — e.g. missing the required `event` field, or with a `level` outside the enum — is classified malformed by REUSING core validate('JournalRecord', parsed) (types.ts:1383 / SCHEMAS.JournalRecord :1260) and its reason carries the validator's own error strings; replay hand-rolls no field checks. Asserted with a mutation-proof pair: one line failing on a missing required key and one failing on the level enum

readRunJournal on a run dir holding journal.2.jsonl.gz, journal.1.jsonl.gz and journal.jsonl returns the records of ALL THREE, ordered journal.1 then journal.2 then the active journal.jsonl (ascending archive index first, active file last), inflating the archives with node:zlib gunzipSync — the same module adapter/journal.ts:28 imports and :216 gzipped them with. Its `sources` list names the three files in that order

an archive that is not valid gzip (or is unreadable) is reported as a failed source with its filename and the error, the records of every other source still render, and the process exits 0 — a partially readable history is still worth reading, and dropping the archive silently would make the timeline lie about what happened

ordering is SOURCE ORDER, never a sort by seq or ts: on a fixture where the archived journal.1.jsonl.gz ends at seq 900 and journal.jsonl restarts at seq 1 (the real behaviour — adapter/journal.ts:219 truncates the active file on rotation and :101-121 readLastSeq then returns 0), the rendered timeline shows the archived records BEFORE the restarted ones, and the recorded seq values are printed verbatim including the duplicates

deriveSwimlanes returns one lane per distinct itemId in FIRST-APPEARANCE order, preceded by exactly one run-level lane (itemId null) holding every record that carries no itemId; within each lane the records keep their input order. Asserted on a fixture interleaving run-level and I1/I2/I3 records so neither grouping nor ordering can pass by accident

conservation law: every record handed to deriveSwimlanes appears EXACTLY ONCE across all lanes — the summed lane lengths equal the input length and the multiset of (seq, component, event) tuples is identical — so no record can be silently dropped by a grouping bug. A record whose itemId is the empty string is treated as run-level, not as a lane named '' (adapter/tools.ts:1707-1716 dispatches the plan-review lens jobs with itemId: '', so such records really occur)

a component 'gates' / event 'deny' record (level warn, data {toolName, args, reason} plus optional {command, editPath} per adapter/tools.ts:207-224) is rendered with the literal DENY marker in its swimlane row AND listed in a denials section showing toolName, reason and the command/editPath when present; a 'gates'/'gate-crash' record (level error, data.guarded + data.error, tools.ts:240-252) is marked CRASH and listed in the same section under its own distinct marker. The two markers are different strings and each is asserted independently

the rendered output contains no ANSI escape sequence anywhere (asserted by scanning the whole render for the ESC byte 0x1B), for every fixture including the highlighted denials — highlighting is plain ASCII markers, so a render piped into a file, a diff or a bug report stays byte-clean and G1 needs no color dependency

deriveFanoutRows pairs each fanout 'subsession.dispatched' record with the NEXT terminal record for the same sessionID ('subsession.complete' or 'subsession.abort'), producing one row carrying sessionID, role/itemId/tree/model from the dispatched payload (fanout.ts:281-289), durationMs computed as terminal.ts minus dispatched.ts, the attempt count derived from the 'subsession.retry' records between them (fanout.ts:304), and an outcome taken from the terminal record's data (ok:true, or reason 'schema-invalid' / 'engine-error' / 'watchdog-timeout'). The duration is computed from the journal, because FanoutResult.timings (fanout.ts:66-71) is returned to the caller and never written to the journal

records whose sessionID is ABSENT or the EMPTY STRING are never merged into one synthetic session: a fixture with two watchdog aborts emitted during the create phase (fanout.ts:196/:200/:231-238 — corr() carries sessionID "" before session.create returns) plus one 'session-create-failed' complete (fanout.ts:265-273 — no sessionID at all) yields THREE separate unpaired rows, each marked as having no session and no fabricated duration, never a single row and never a pairing with an unrelated dispatch

a dispatched record with no terminal record (the crash/kill case) renders as an explicit unterminated row with NO duration value — not 0, not a now()-minus-start figure — so a run that died mid-wave is visibly distinguishable from one whose sub-sessions completed instantly; and a 'subsession.hold' record (fanout.ts:355-362, no sessionID) is counted as a hold against its item rather than being dropped or mistaken for a dispatch

deriveReviewRounds produces one row per review round, subject = record.itemId ?? 'plan', from the records committed producers actually emit: 'fsm'/'guard-reject' with data.stage present (adapter/tools.ts:1913-1927 — round, max, findings, survivingMajors, why) is a round that DID NOT pass, and 'fsm'/'transition' carrying data.survivingMajors (tools.ts:2053-2068 — rounds, lenses, findingsRaised {major,minor,nit}) closes the sequence. Asserted on a two-round fixture: row 1 shows round 1 with its surviving majors and a re-round outcome, row 2 shows the accepted round with its findingsRaised breakdown, and the reviewer/skeptic sub-session counts in each round's window come from the fan-out rows between that round's boundaries. The derivation reads BOTH key spellings (`round` vs `rounds`, `findings` vs `findingsRaised`) rather than assuming one shape

the lens column is filled from data.lens on the dispatched record when present, else from the round's data.lenses roster (tools.ts:2060), else rendered as unknown — never invented. Asserted three ways on one fixture: a dispatched record carrying lens renders that lens; a dispatched record without one inside a round whose transition carries a lenses roster renders the roster; and a reviewer dispatch with neither renders the unknown marker while still counting toward the round's reviewer total (the committed producer at fanout.ts:281-289 omits job.lens even though FanoutJob:63 carries it — see SG-4)

the review section contains NO per-finding uphold/overturn column and never reads runs/<runId>/reviews/*.json — verified absent at HEAD (no writer exists in conductor/{core,adapter,tools}) — asserted by running the renderer inside a run dir whose reviews/ directory is present but populated with a file that would crash a reader: the render succeeds unchanged and the file is never opened. A renderer reports what the journal recorded and nothing else (G4: no stub reader for an unwritten artifact)

the --level filter is a THRESHOLD, not an exact match: --level warn keeps error and warn records and drops info/debug/trace; --level trace keeps everything; absent --level filters nothing. The severity order is the single exported core list (core/types.ts LOG_LEVELS, exported by this task per SG-2, error most severe) and replay declares no order of its own — asserted by comparing replay's ordering to the imported list rather than to a literal array in the test

--component and --item each accept repetition AND comma-separated values, unioned within a flag ('--component fanout --component gates' and '--component fanout,gates' select the same records), and the three flags compose as AND: '--component fanout --item I2 --level info' keeps exactly the fanout records for item I2 at info or above. --item excludes records carrying no itemId (they belong to the run lane, not to an item), asserted on a fixture where a run-level gates/deny record is present and must NOT appear under --item I2

filters are applied ONCE and every section derives from that same filtered set: with '--component gates' the fan-out duration table and the review-round table are EMPTY (and say so explicitly rather than being omitted), and with '--item I2' the duration table holds only I2's sub-sessions. A section that quietly re-read the unfiltered records would make two halves of one render disagree about what happened

a record whose data is the journal's truncation marker — {truncated:true} or {truncated:true, preview:…} as written by adapter/journal.ts:142-159 when a record exceeds the 32 KiB cap at :58 — renders with an explicit TRUNCATED marker (and the preview when present), never as an empty or absent payload: a silently blank data field reads as 'nothing happened' when in fact the payload was too big to keep

a record whose component+event is outside the closed §7.4 vocabulary — the shape adapter/journal.ts:228-240 deliberately RETAINS in production rather than dropping — is rendered in its lane with an explicit unknown-event marker, decided by REUSING core isKnownEvent (journal-events.ts:66); it is neither hidden nor treated as malformed, because the record is on disk precisely so a human can see it

renderTimeline is deterministic and clock-free: called twice on the same input it returns byte-identical strings; timestamps are rendered from record.ts as ISO-8601 UTC (asserted by rendering a fixture and finding the exact expected UTC string, which pins that no local timezone or locale formatting is used); and the output contains no wall-clock text such as a generation timestamp. The pure functions never call Date.now(), so two machines in two timezones produce the same render of the same journal

the argv shell (SG-7): no run-dir argument, an unknown flag, an unknown --component value or an unknown --level value each yield parseArgs {ok:false} with exitCode 2 and a message naming the offending value — and for --component the message lists the eight legal components taken from core COMPONENTS (journal-events.ts:16), so a typo can never render a silently empty timeline; a run dir with no journal.jsonl and no archives yields exit 1 naming the path; a run dir whose journal exists but is empty exits 0 and renders an explicit zero-record notice. Usage errors write to stderr and produce NO stdout

replay mutates nothing: after readRunJournal + renderTimeline over a fixture run dir, every file in that dir is byte-identical and no file has been created or removed (asserted by comparing a full recursive name+content snapshot taken before and after). It dispatches zero model sub-sessions, opens no network connection, and reads no state file — journal.jsonl and its archives are its only inputs (§13:3200 names replay the journal's reader)

the fixture cannot drift from reality: a journal produced by the COMMITTED writer — createJournal (adapter/journal.ts:161) driven to emit a gates/deny, a fanout dispatched/complete pair and an fsm transition, then flushSync — is read back by readRunJournal with zero malformed lines, and the derived denial, duration and review sections match the records that were logged. This is the row that fails if the writer's shape and the reader's expectations ever part company
